title: Canary forensics panel — CauseFinder + rollback playbook
creator: Maya Singh
description: Build a dedicated Console panel that surfaces canary rollout forensics: linked traces, per-route metric diffs between cohorts, heatmaps of feature/regression signals, and a guided rollback playbook. The panel should prioritize fast root-cause discovery for small-scale canaries and provide actionable auto-rollback signals that tie to policy rules.
background: Teams running canaries and A/B experiments lack a single surface in Console that correlates per-route latency/error deltas with trace evidence and downstream cost/quality signals. Existing dashboards show per-route p95 and token cost, but switching between traces, cohort diffs, and rollout controls is manual and slows incident decision-making. This ticket scopes a focused UI + backend contract to bridge metrics, traces, and policy-driven rollback triggers.
goals: Expose per-route cohort diffs (p50/p95/error-rate/token-cost) in a compact heatmap
Surface 1-click linked traces for the largest regressions by cohort
Provide an evidence panel (CauseFinder) that summarizes top contributing factors (route, model variant, prompt size, quantization profile)
Integrate auto-rollback policy preview and runbook actions in the same panel
Make metrics queryable with time-window and baseline controls and exportable as CSV
non_goals: Full experiment statistics engine (bayesian inference) — out of scope for MVP
Replacing existing tracing UX — link through to APM for deep trace analysis
Implementing automated model retraining or tuning
success_metrics: MTTR for canary regressions reduced by 40% within 8 weeks of rollout
>75% of canary incidents have an actionable trace link from the panel
Reduced manual rollbacks (via CLI) by 30% as teams use in-console rollback actions
Panel adoption: 60% of mid/enterprise teams use the panel for canaries within the quarter
data_sources: Per-route metrics: existing metrics pipeline (Prometheus -> BigQuery aggregated tables)
Trace links: OpenTelemetry traces stored in Jaeger/OTLP backend (link by trace_id)
Model-variant annotation: model_id + version from rollout metadata service
Token-level cost: tokenizer-cost delta from billing telemetry
Canary config: rollout metadata service (cohort definitions, traffic weights, policy rules)
backend_contracts: New API: GET /api/observability/canaries/{canary_id}/cohort-diff?window=5m returns per-route delta vectors
New API: GET /api/observability/canaries/{canary_id}/top-traces?limit=25 returns sample trace_ids with reason tags
New table: canary_signals.daily_aggregates (date, canary_id, route, cohort, p50,p95,error_rate,cost_per_token)
Instrument: attach model_variant and rollout_id to traces at request ingress for causal linking
acceptance_criteria: UI shows heatmap of per-route p95 and error-rate diffs between control and canary for selected time window
Clicking a bad cell opens an evidence pane with top 3 trace links and a short summary of contributing factors
Teams can preview auto-rollback policy conditions and trigger a dry-run action that simulates rollback decision output
Export button produces CSV with route-level metrics and cohort delta for the selected window
Backend APIs have metrics (latency, error) and are covered by integration tests; docs for API contract exist in Confluence

Eng: Implement cohort-diff aggregation endpoint and daily aggregate table (owner: Priya Kapoor) — estimate 5
Eng: Expose top-trace sampler API and ensure trace_id propagation (owner: Daniel Kim) — estimate 3

notes: Trade-offs: real-time per-request diffing is expensive — MVP will rely on short-window aggregates (1m/5m) and sample traces
Auto-rollback policy should be conservative for first release (require two independent signals: metric delta + trace-based error spike)
Privacy: traces may include PII; front-end must preserve trace redaction and only surface trace_ids and summary fields
Rollout plan: start with internal alpha teams, then opt-in beta with 3 customers before org-wide release
